poem:
## The Sprue-Tree's Lament

'Twas sprue, and the waxy wicks
Did gangle and gleam in the vat.
All glimmery were the sprue-sticks,
And the wax-worms did skitter and plat.

"Beware the Sprue-Tree, my son!
The branches that twist, the roots that entwine!
Beware the mold-slug, and shun
The jabbering of the Wax-Mine!"

He took his sprue-knife in hand;
Long time the Sprue-Tree foe he sought—
So rested he by the slag-stand,
And pondered in thoughtful thought.

And, as in molten thought he stood,
The Sprue-Tree, with eyes of fire,
Came whiffling through the sprue-wood,
And goggled with dire desire!

One, two! One, two! And through and through
The sprue-knife went snicker-snack!
He left it dead, and with its screw
He went galumphing back.

"And hast thou slain the Sprue-Tree?
Come to my arms, my beamish boy!
O frabjous day! Callooh! Callay!"
He chortled in his joy.

'Twas sprue, and the waxy wicks
Did gangle and gleam in the vat.
All glimmery were the sprue-sticks,
And the wax-worms did skitter and plat.

'Twas brillig, and the china-ware
Did fracture in the scullery,
All shardy were the cups, and there
Did gleam the shards of pottery.

"Beware the Kintsug, my son!
The joins that bind, the flaws that shine!
Beware the Crumblesome, and shun
The shattering, the fine-spun line!"

He took his trusty brush in hand;
Long time the broken foe he sought—
So rested he by the mending stand,
And stood a-mending, lost in thought.

And, as in polished thought he stood,
The Kintsug, with its golden gleam,
Came mending through the broken wood,
And bubbled, like a gilded stream!

One, two! One, two! And through and through
The brush went glinting, mending fast!
It left it bright, and golden-new,
And left it mended, built to last.

"And hast thou joined the Kintsug then?
Come to my arms, my mending boy!
O frabjous day! Callooh! Callay!"
He chortled in his joy.

'Twas brillig, and the china-ware
Did fracture in the scullery,
All shardy were the cups, and there
Did gleam the shards of pottery.

He left it dead, and with its hue
He went galumphing back.

"And hast thou slain the Scree-Glow?
Come to my arms, my beamish boy!
O frabjous day! Callooh! Callay!"
He chortled in his joy.

'Twas alpenglow, and the slippy scree
Did tumble and crumble with mizzling sound;
All glidgy were the rocks, and he
Did scrabble and stumble around.
